market_name: Will OpenAI not IPO by December 31, 2026?

trade_eligibility.reason: Below minimum expected move or unclear direction.

time_plan.30m: Check whether the prediction-market probability actually moved sharply (>10pts) and whether any IPO/S-1 headline or Microsoft-OpenAI restructuring news is circulating.
time_plan.1h: Compare MSFT intraday move vs. QQQ/SOX to isolate any idiosyncratic AI-stake repricing from broad tech beta.
time_plan.2h: Scan for confirming reporting (Bloomberg/Reuters/WSJ) on OpenAI IPO timing or valuation; if none, treat market move as noise.
time_plan.6h: Reassess whether MSFT drift persists or mean-reverts; check options skew for unusual AI-related positioning.
time_plan.12h: Log realized MSFT return vs. expectation; conclude whether the prediction market carried any leading information or was pure noise.

predictions.reasoning: Microsoft is OpenAI's largest strategic partner and holds a substantial equity stake, so any sharp shift in the implied probability of an OpenAI IPO (and its implied valuation) could theoretically re-rate MSFT's embedded AI optionality. A rising IPO probability at a high valuation would crystallize/mark up the value of MSFT's stake (mild positive); however, an IPO could also dilute Microsoft's future economics or signal a governance shift, making the sign genuinely ambiguous. Crucially, this is a slow-moving structural corporate-finance question with a 14-month horizon, not a catalyst likely to move a $3T+ mega-cap within any given 12h window.

trade_eligibility.reason: Below minimum expected move or unclear direction.

time_plan.30m: Verify no dominant macro catalyst (rates, econ data) is driving tech; isolate whether any AI-specific narrative shift exists.
time_plan.1h: Watch NVDA and semis relative strength as the purer AI-sentiment tell vs. QQQ.
time_plan.2h: Check for credible IPO reporting; absent it, downgrade any thesis to noise.
time_plan.6h: Reassess whether AI-basket outperformance is holding vs. broad market.
time_plan.12h: Record realized QQQ move and whether an AI-narrative channel was even plausibly active.

predictions.reasoning: A concrete, high-valuation OpenAI IPO path would validate the AI capex/monetization narrative broadly, providing mild sentiment support to large-cap tech (Nvidia, Microsoft, semiconductor supply chain). But the linkage from a probability shift on IPO *timing* to a diversified index over 12 hours is very weak and easily swamped by macro (rates, CPI, Fed) and index-level flows. Direction is genuinely unclear because an IPO can be read as bullish validation or as a top-signal/liquidity-drain for private AI capital.

evidence_used: Market question concerns OpenAI IPO occurrence and first-day valuation by Dec 31, 2026 — a 14-month structural horizon
Microsoft is OpenAI's largest external investor and cloud partner, the most direct listed proxy
No specific catalyst, S-1 filing, or dated event is embedded in the question itself
uncertainty_notes: The event horizon (end-2026) is far outside the 12h prediction window, so probability moves are unlikely to have same-day asset impact
The sign of an IPO's effect on Microsoft is ambiguous (stake mark-up vs. dilution/governance change)
No liquid pure-play OpenAI proxy exists; MSFT exposure is fractional relative to its total market cap
A probability move could reflect speculation/thin liquidity on Polymarket rather than leaked information

llm_justification.summary: This market asks whether OpenAI will avoid an IPO through end-2026 — a long-horizon corporate-finance question with no clean, liquid public proxy. The best-available proxies (Microsoft as largest investor, and a broad AI/tech basket via QQQ) have only fractional, ambiguously-signed exposure. Given the 14-month event horizon versus a 12h window, any move is far below the 700bp tradable threshold, direction is unclear, and confidence is low. This is a weak mapping best flagged as noise rather than signal.
key_assumptions: Microsoft remains OpenAI's most material listed stakeholder
A sharp prediction-market probability shift would be the only 'signal' to act on
AI-narrative sentiment can transmit to tech indices, if weakly
failure_modes: The IPO timing has no measurable 12h effect on mega-cap proxies (most likely outcome)
The move is already public/priced or reflects thin prediction-market liquidity, not leaked info
The proxy (MSFT/QQQ) is far too diversified to register an OpenAI-specific repricing
Sign is wrong: an IPO could be read as dilutive/top-signal rather than value-accretive
Macro factors (rates, data prints) dominate any AI-narrative channel over the window
llm_justification.why_not_ex_post: The card is timestamped, content-hashed, and never overwritten. Execution must reject any card created after an anomaly's trigger time.
